name: Uri
overview: Uri was a male Levite who served as a gatekeeper. He is notably identified as having married a foreign wife, an issue addressed in the post-exilic community. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Uri means 'y-h-v-h is [my] flame, light,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the Lord as a source of illumination. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:24.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Uri as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the tribe set apart for religious duties. No further familial relationships beyond this tribal affiliation and his foreign wife are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Uri's significance lies in his role as a Levite gatekeeper who was involved in the post-exilic reforms concerning intermarriage with foreign women. His inclusion in Ezra 10:24 highlights the community's efforts to maintain covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands during the restoration period. Uri exemplifies the challenges faced by returning exiles in upholding holiness within the restored Israelite community.
